images.title: Exterior angle
images.purpose: Show an exterior angle of a triangle and that it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
images.composition: One triangle on the left, with its base extended to the right to make the exterior angle, and a short sum caption below.
exact_structure: Triangle ABC with B at the left on a horizontal base, C at the right on the base, A above; angle at A is 50° (teal #0072B2 arc), angle at B is 60° (amber #E69F00 arc), angle at C inside the triangle is 70° (grey #6B7280 arc).
The base BC extended to the right past C as a dashed line ending at D.
The exterior angle ACD, between CA and CD, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) and labelled 110°.
rejection: an exterior angle that is not on the extension of BC
the inside angles not being 50°, 60° and 70°
the exterior angle labelled with a value other than 110°
images.takeaway: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.
images.description: Triangle ABC with angles 50°, 60° and 70° and its exterior angle at C marked 110°.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Point to the purple exterior angle, then to the teal and amber angles that add up to it.

image_decisions.why: The exterior angle is the one idea; the sum caption is its rule.
